comparator.name: Bachelor Mechanical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, degree-structure, Education Guide and 2026-2027 course-catalogue records, checked 2026-10-05, describe a three-year, 180-EC Mechanical Engineering bachelor for students starting in 2023-2024 or later. The degree comprises 120 EC of mechanical-engineering major and Bachelor College core formation, including challenge-based projects and the Bachelor Final Project, plus a 60-EC elective part consisting of a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of electives. The complete 120/15/45 allocation is retained below rather than assigning unsupported individual credit values to the public course records.
components: Mechanical Engineering major and Bachelor College core programme, including Bachelor Final Project

Compulsory formation in mathematics, mechanics, statics and dynamics, strength and structures, thermodynamics, heat and fluid flow, transport phenomena, materials, manufacturing, measurement, modelling, signals, dynamics and control, mechatronics, computer-aided engineering, repeated engineering-design projects and the Bachelor Final Project.
Genuine programme choice within the official elective part.
Genuine elective space preserved from the official curriculum structure.

exception.reason: Mechanical Engineering at TU/e is a cumulative physical-engineering degree. Its compulsory formation progresses from calculus, mechanics, statics and dynamics through solid and structural mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid flow and transport phenomena, materials and manufacturing, measurement, modelling, signals, system dynamics and control, mechatronics and computer-aided engineering, integrating these fields in repeated design and experimental projects before a discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers relevant mathematics, programming, linear systems, robotics, sustainable-energy analysis and one consumer-product-design course. It does not offer the required mechanics sequence, thermodynamics and fluid-mechanics progression, materials and manufacturing formation, engineering measurement and experimental laboratories, machine-component and precision-design sequence, mechatronic hardware integration, repeated mechanical-design projects or an equivalent mechanical-engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR response would be a mathematics-and-computing programme with robotics, energy and design applications, not a defensible Mechanical Engineering comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official current structure accounts for all 180 EC as 120 EC of Mechanical Engineering major and Bachelor College core formation, including the Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of electives. Current 2026-2027 course records confirm the programme's integrated spine in introductory mechanical engineering and truss structures, mechanics, dynamics, strength and structure, thermodynamics, heat and flow, materials, mechanical-system dynamics and control, and advanced engineering design. These domains are progressively combined in analysis, experimentation, modelling and design rather than offered as independent optional applications of mathematics or computation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide useful quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics provide programming, modelling, perception and general control applications. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design add energy-system context, while BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design adds one team-based product-development and prototyping experience. The workbook nevertheless contains no engineering-physics or mechanics sequence, statics, kinematics and machine dynamics, strength of materials and structural analysis, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics and transport phenomena, engineering materials, manufacturing processes, mechanical measurements and experimental mechanics, vibration analysis, machine elements, precision engineering, computer-aided mechanical engineering, mechatronic hardware laboratory, or repeated mechanical-system design and capstone projects. DISMATH312 studies mathematical linear systems but cannot replace physical system dynamics, mechanics, measurement and control implementation. DISDATA312 covers general robotics rather than the target's staged mechanics, actuation, sensing, mechatronic integration and machine design. BENENTR111 is one valuable product-development course but cannot replace the target's cumulative analysis, fabrication, laboratory and engineering-design spine. The available UCR courses therefore support robotics, energy or technology themes while leaving the defining mechanical-engineering formation unmatched.
